understanding.purpose: השוואת דירות להשכרה בתל אביב לפי שכונה, מחיר, מספר חדרים, קומה ומאפיינים נוספים.
understanding.reading: הקוראים סורקים מימין לשמאל את פרטי כל דירה ומשווים בין שורות, במיוחד לפי מחיר ומספר חדרים. ההערות מספקות הקשר להחלטה, ויכולות להגדיל את גובה השורה; שטח זה יכול לשמש גם לגלישה טבעית בעמודות אחרות.
groups: מחיר וחדרים הם נתונים קצרים המשמשים להשוואה ישירה בין דירות.
קומה והערות מתארות את מאפייני הדירה והבניין; פרטי המעלית מופיעים לצד הקומה.
השכונה מזהה כל שורה ומשמשת נקודת עוגן לסריקה.
keep_intact: שמות שכונות ומילים בודדות צריכים להישאר שלמים.
מספרי המחיר, מספרי החדרים והמספרים בתיאור הקומה צריכים להישאר שלמים.
may_wrap: הערות ארוכות יכולות להישבר בין מילים למשפטים קריאים.
תיאור הקומה והמעלית יכול להישבר בין חלקיו.
יחידת הזמן במחיר יכולה לעבור לשורה נפרדת מן הסכום.

bad.why: The floor column is much wider than its short entries need, leaving the long notes cramped into many short lines. The resulting tall rows make both the notes and comparisons across apartments harder to scan.

contrast.why: The floor column is much wider than its short entries need, leaving the long notes cramped into many short lines. The resulting tall rows make both the notes and comparisons across apartments harder to scan.

final.rationale: In r2C, neighborhood names and room counts stay on one line, while the price wraps consistently after the amount. The floor entries mostly fit in two lines, and the generous notes column keeps five of the six data rows to three lines. This gives the table a steady row rhythm without squeezing the descriptive text.

general: Give long prose enough width to form readable phrases, while reserving enough space for frequently compared values and row identifiers.
Consistent wrapping can support scanning, but splitting a short meaningful phrase across several lines makes comparison harder.
Judge width distribution by the role and content of each column rather than seeking equal widths or minimum table height.
specific: The notes are substantially longer than the other entries, so they deserve about half the available width.
At 105px, the floor column avoids the three-line wrapping seen in some entries at 90px; the price can wrap consistently at 85px.

final.tradeoffs: A wider price column keeps the amount and monthly unit together, as in r3B, but reduces space for notes and makes several rows taller. A wider notes column, as in r3C, improves prose width at the cost of splitting some floor descriptions over three lines.
final.uncertain: The ranges are conservative visual estimates, not browser-tested thresholds. They assume that width changes are compensated across the other columns in roughly their existing proportions and that the total stays within 719px; small changes can alter individual line breaks.

A.why: Neighborhoods and monthly prices stay on one line, rooms are compact, and the notes have enough width for readable paragraphs. Floor details wrap consistently without obscuring their meaning.

B.why: Equal-width columns leave large empty areas around short values while squeezing notes into very narrow, tall paragraphs. The resulting row heights make comparisons difficult.

C.why: The notes read comfortably, but several neighborhood names wrap, as do all prices and some floor details. That weakens the scan of the main comparison columns.

D.why: Floor details fit on one line, but their column has substantial unused space while notes wrap into narrow, tall blocks. The long rows make it harder to connect each description with its listing.

E.why: Neighborhoods stay intact and the notes have comfortable line lengths. Prices and floor details wrap consistently, though the split monthly price makes comparison a little less immediate.

F.why: Neighborhoods stay intact and the generous notes column keeps most descriptions to three lines. Prices and floor details wrap, trading some scan speed for shorter rows.

reviews.unsure: A keeps the main comparison values together, while F gives the longer descriptions more room and produces shorter rows. The preference depends on how much weight readers place on scanning prices versus reading notes.

A.why: Neighborhood names stay intact and the notes have comfortable line lengths. Prices and floor details wrap consistently, though both require extra lines.

B.why: A generous notes column supports easy reading, while neighborhood names remain intact. Prices and floor details wrap onto two lines, but the rows still scan well.

C.why: The narrow notes column produces tall blocks of short lines, while the much wider rooms and neighborhood columns contain large stretches of empty space. Rows are difficult to scan across.

D.why: Notes read comfortably, but two neighborhood names wrap and some floor details spread over three lines. That weakens scanning of the row identifiers and key comparisons.

E.why: Prices and floor details fit on one line, but the oversized floor column leaves substantial empty space while notes wrap into tall, narrow blocks.

F.why: Neighborhoods and prices stay on one line, floor details wrap predictably, and notes have enough width for readable lines. The columns balance comparison with room for descriptive text.

reviews.unsure: B gives the notes more room, so a reader prioritizing the descriptions might prefer it; F keeps the full price on one line and balances the columns more evenly.
